newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House passes major securities bill.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House passes major securities bill.

text.p: The House late Saturday passed a landmark securities reform bill reducing burdensome regulations and saving $850 million over five years in government fees.
The compromise bill was sent to the Senate for final congressional action.
The House voice vote on the measure followed agreement by a Senate-House conference committee on oversight of the nation's 150,000 investment advisers.
Under the agreement states will regulate individual advisers and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) will oversee firms, an aide said.
Rep Thomas Bliley, R-Virginia, chairman of the Commerce Committee, told the House the first major overhaul of securities law in 50 years would promote efficiency in capital markets.

Rep John Dingell, D-Michigan, supported the bill but said he was disappointed at the investment adviser provisions which he said maintained the "status quo" and lost an opportunity to better police swindlers and incompetents who got rich at the expense of small investors.
Rep Edward Markey, D-Massachusetts, said that under the bill, investors would be able to call a 1-800 number for information of investment advisers' records.
A conference statement on the bill said it eliminated burdens and enhanced innovation and efficieny for investment companies.

The legislation gives the SEC additional authority over investment company books and records and preparation of shareholder reports. The SEC would be allowed to examine only records it requires investment companies to maintain for inspection.
The drafters of the bill said they intended that over a 10-year period the SEC would collect fees equal to the cost of running the agency.
